issues.description: The problem text instructs students to implement singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) as public, but the UML diagram in the same problem statement marks singFarmSongVerse as private (prefixed with '-') and both the template and the solution implement singFarmSongVerse as private. This contradiction in the problem statement (text vs UML) and the template/solution visibility will confuse students about the intended accessibility of the helper method and may cause tests or expectations to diverge.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended visibility consistent across artifacts: either update the problem statement text to state the helper is private (matching the UML, template, and solution), or change the template and solution method declarations to public (public void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) so they match the textual instruction and tests that expect a public helper.

issues.description: The template's singFarmSongVerse method has no parameter (it is declared as singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) without an Animal parameter), while the problem statement and the solution expect a parameter singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). The missing parameter in the template is a structural mismatch that prevents students from implementing or calling the method as specified and will lead to compile-time/signature mismatches with the expected solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the Animal parameter to the template method signature to match the specification and solution: change the template declaration to (public) void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and update its body to use the animal parameter. Ensure the visibility chosen matches the clarified instruction (see previous issue).
